title: Seasonal Recharge of a Shallow Alluvial Aquifer

headings.text: Seasonal Recharge of a Shallow Alluvial Aquifer

key_sentences: Shallow alluvial aquifers supply most of the drinking water in the villages of the lower valley.
Little is known about how quickly the water table responds after the first heavy rain.
We monitored twelve wells twice a week from May to November.
The water table rose by an average of 2.4 m within ten days of the first storm.
The recession constant was remarkably similar across all twelve wells.
These results suggest that the aquifer is recharged mainly through the riverbed rather than by direct infiltration.
notes: Font Times New Roman 11.5pt, paragraphs justified (inter-word spaces vary), no hyphenation. Author line 'R. Okonjo and L. Varga' (centred, italic) is neither a heading nor a key sentence. FOOTNOTE MARKERS: superscript '1' after 'riverbed.' in the Introduction and superscript '2' after 'wells.' in the Method; both sentences are left OUT of key_sentences. The footnotes sit at the bottom of the text under a short rule: '1 Infiltration was estimated from double-ring tests at six points.' and '2 The station is operated by the district agricultural office.' (each starts with a superscript number). INLINE FORMULA in the Method paragraph, left out of key_sentences: visually 'h(t) = h0 · e^(−kt)' - h, t and k italic, '0' is a subscript, '−kt' is a superscript and the minus is U+2212, the dot is U+00B7; the sentence reads 'The decline of the water level after the last rain was fitted with the exponential model h(t) = h0 · e−kt, where k is the recession constant.' when sub/superscripts are flattened. Furniture: running header 'Sahel Water Studies 7(2), 2026' (top right, italic, ruled below) and page number '41' (bottom centre). Serif text may carry fi/fl ligatures depending on the font ('infiltration', 'fitted').
